seo.title: CyberSuivi GAT — Cybersecurity awareness platform (case study)
seo.description: How I built CyberSuivi GAT at GAT Assurances: Power BI dashboards, a phishing-risk Random Forest model (AUC 0.91), a secure web platform and the CyberBot AI assistant.

header.title: CyberSuivi GAT
header.tagline: A cybersecurity awareness platform that turns training, quiz and phishing data into strategic decisions and individual risk predictions.

kpis.label: tailored experiences (Executive Committee, IT Security team)

problem.title: The problem
problem.text: Before CyberSuivi, awareness data lived in static Excel files, scattered across sources. The company had no way to see the overall security posture, and no way to identify which employees were most at risk of falling for phishing.

pillars.title: Business Intelligence
pillars.text: Power BI dashboards to monitor awareness and support decisions.

pillars.title: Machine Learning
pillars.text: A model that predicts each employee's phishing risk.

pillars.title: Web Platform
pillars.text: One secure application that centralises every feature.

pillars.title: AI Assistant
pillars.text: CyberBot answers any cybersecurity question instantly.

audiences.title: Two audiences, two experiences

cards.title: Executive Committee
cards.text: Access to a single global dashboard only. A clear, high-level view of the organisation's security posture to make strategic decisions.

cards.title: IT Security Team
cards.text: Full access to every feature of the platform, to act at the employee level.

audiences.note: Role-based access control (JWT) and Power BI Row-Level Security make sure each audience sees only what it needs.

features.title: Features for the IT Security team

items.title: Cyber threat watch
items.text: A live feed of cybersecurity news (NewsAPI), so the team stays up to date on new threats.

items.title: Detailed tracking per employee
items.text: Quizzes, trainings, simulated phishing campaigns, and a computed vulnerability score.

items.title: Phishing risk prediction
items.text: A machine-learning model predicts each employee's risk, so the team can target training where it matters most.

items.title: CyberBot
items.text: An AI assistant powered by Groq (Llama 3.3 70B). The security team can ask any cybersecurity question and get an instant answer. A pandas-based analytics engine returns exact figures from the platform's data.

model.title: Kimball constellation schema
model.text: Kimball methodology, constellation schema with 4 fact tables (quizzes, trainings, phishing, vulnerability) and shared dimensions (employees, departments, quizzes, trainings, campaigns).

etl.title: ETL and refresh
etl.text: ETL with Power Query, automated refresh from a shared OneDrive/SharePoint folder.

score.title: Vulnerability score out of 100
score.text: One score per employee, built from three axes.

dax.title: DAX measures
dax.text: DAX measures for scoring, status and root cause, with dynamic titles.

model.title: Random Forest classifier
model.text: Random Forest classifier predicting phishing click risk.

split.title: Temporal anti-leakage split
split.text: Features for year N are computed only from previous years, to predict year N+1.

shap.title: SHAP explainability
shap.text: The team can see why an employee is flagged.

lesson.title: Lesson learned
lesson.text: An early version reached a suspicious 100% accuracy. I diagnosed it as data leakage and redesigned the pipeline around temporal prediction.

demo.title: Try the risk predictor
demo.intro: Move the sliders to see how a profile changes the predicted risk.
demo.disclaimer: Simplified demo with synthetic data — the production model is a Random Forest trained on real (confidential) data.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.powerbiNote: Embedded in the platform with Row-Level Security

results.title: Results
items: The Power BI solution is deployed in production at GAT Assurances.
The full web platform is being deployed by GAT's infrastructure team.

learned.title: What I learned
items: Designing one product for two very different audiences: executives and technical teams.
Spotting and fixing data leakage: a model that looks perfect is often wrong.
Connecting BI, ML, web and AI into a single coherent platform.
